title: The Taliesin Massacre
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss Frank Lloyd Wright's Taliesin estate in Spring Green, Wisconsin, and the 1914 Taliesin massacre. They cover Wright's Prairie style and his personal life, including his 1909 departure to Europe with Mamah Borthwick Cheney, his return and the cottage built on family land, and the August 15, 1914 attack in which handyman Julian Carlton killed Borthwick, her two children, and several employees, then set the house on fire. They touch on Carlton's death in jail, Wright's later marriages to Miriam Noel and Olga Lazovic Hinzenburg, his later work including Taliesin West, and the hosts' companion book. The episode opens with banter about Wright's buildings and closes with a book plug and sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter on Frank Lloyd Wright and his buildings
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode as a Frank Lloyd Wright edition and trade thoughts on Wright's houses they have visited, the Guggenheim, and their feelings about Prairie style and modern homes.

segments.title: Taliesin's history and design
segments.summary: Taliesin is described as Wright's home, studio, and school on an 800-acre family estate in Wisconsin, built in the Prairie style with cantilevered roofs and no gutters, and completed around 1911.

segments.title: Wright's affair with Mamah Borthwick Cheney
segments.summary: Wright met Mamah Borthwick Cheney in 1903 when he designed a house for her and her husband Edwin Cheney. The affair began around 1907 while Wright was tired of his Prairie work and had six children with his wife Kitty.

segments.title: Wright leaves for Europe and returns to Chicago
segments.summary: In September 1909 Wright left his family for Europe with Mamah, drawing headlines. He returned in 1910 while she stayed to finish her divorce, and he was treated as a pariah by his social circle.

segments.title: Darwin Martin's money and the cottage at Taliesin
segments.summary: Wright obtained funds from benefactor Darwin Martin to build a cottage for his mother, and moved in with Mamah around 1911. Wright never repaid Martin, who later lost his fortune in the stock market crash.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the murders are discussed.

segments.title: The August 1914 Taliesin massacre
segments.summary: On August 15, 1914, handyman Julian Carlton, who had been acting erratically, attacked the lunch gathering at Taliesin with an axe and gasoline. He killed Mamah Borthwick, her two children, and several employees, and set the house on fire. Herb Fritz and David Lindblom escaped through a window, and Lindblom later died of burns. Carlton drank hydrochloric acid and was found in the boiler room, and he died in jail seven weeks later. John Lloyd Wright learned of the attack by phone while in Chicago.

segments.title: Wright's later marriages and the Mann Act arrest
segments.summary: After the massacre Wright struggled professionally. He married Miriam Noel in 1923, which ended quickly, and later married Olga Lazovic Hinzenburg in 1928. Miriam had Wright arrested under the Mann Act and later tried to undermine his second marriage.

segments.title: Taliesin West and later works
segments.summary: The hosts note Wright's most productive period from the 1930s until his death in 1959, including Taliesin West in Scottsdale, Arizona, and Florida Southern College. They plan future episodes on Wright.

segments.title: Book plug and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts promote their book, Stuff You Should Know: An Incomplete Compendium of Mostly Interesting Things, and describe some of its chapters. They close with contact information and sign off.
